title: Criminal Appeal or Revision: What Is the Difference?
desc: An appeal lets a court re-examine the facts of a conviction; a revision only checks if an order was legal and proper, under the BNSS.
why: People often file a revision expecting the court to weigh the evidence afresh, as in an appeal, and are surprised when the court only checks whether the order itself was legal and proper.
keyPoints: An appeal is a legal right to challenge a conviction or sentence; a revision is not a right but a discretionary power of the court.
An appeal, filed under BNSS section 415 (old CrPC section 374), lets a higher court re-examine the facts, evidence and sentence.
A revision, under BNSS sections 438 and 442 (old CrPC sections 397 and 401), only checks if an order was correct, legal, proper and passed regularly.
A revisional court generally cannot turn an acquittal into a conviction, and cannot be used against every routine, mid-trial order.

sections.h: What is the difference between an appeal and a revision?
p: A criminal appeal under section 415 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS; old CrPC section 374) lets the Sessions Court or the High Court of Uttarakhand re-examine the facts, evidence and sentence of a conviction. A revision under BNSS sections 438 and 442 (old CrPC sections 397 and 401) only lets the court check whether the order was correct, legal and proper, without reassessing the evidence.

An appeal is a statutory right once a person is convicted. A revision is a supervisory power the Sessions Court or High Court uses on its own discretion, mainly to correct a clear illegality or irregularity in a lower court's order.

sections.h: When do you file a revision instead of an appeal?
p: A revision is used when no appeal lies against an order, such as some orders passed by a Magistrate before or during trial that do not amount to a conviction. A Magistrate's order can usually be taken in revision to the Sessions Court first; the High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital is approached after that, or directly where it is a Sessions Court's own order under challenge.

The law does not allow asking the High Court for a revision on the same order after a Sessions Court has already rejected one. The revisional court also cannot convert an acquittal into a conviction, so it is not a route to a full retrial or a higher sentence.

whatToDo: Check first whether an appeal is available as of right; file an appeal, not a revision, if it is.
For a Magistrate's order, apply for revision at the Sessions Court before going to the High Court, unless it is a Sessions Court order itself.
Keep a certified copy of the order and the lower court's record ready, since the revisional court examines the record, not fresh evidence.
Take legal advice on your own facts before choosing between an appeal and a revision, since picking the wrong remedy can waste the limited time you have to file either.

hi.title: आपराधिक अपील और पुनरीक्षण में क्या फ़र्क़ है?
keyPoints: अपील एक अधिकार है; पुनरीक्षण (रिवीज़न) अदालत के विवेक पर निर्भर करता है, यह अधिकार नहीं है।
अपील (बीएनएसएस धारा 415, पुरानी सीआरपीसी धारा 374) में अदालत सबूत और सज़ा दोबारा जाँचती है।
पुनरीक्षण (बीएनएसएस धारा 438 और 442, पुरानी सीआरपीसी धारा 397 और 401) में सिर्फ़ यह देखा जाता है कि आदेश सही, वैध और उचित था या नहीं।
पुनरीक्षण अदालत आमतौर पर बरी होने के फ़ैसले को सज़ा में नहीं बदल सकती।
p: सही रास्ता चुनने से पहले अपने मामले के तथ्यों पर क़ानूनी सलाह लेना बेहतर है, क्योंकि ग़लत रास्ता चुनने से समय सीमा निकल सकती है।
